rules: One idea per hook. If it needs a comma splice, it needs two posts.
Line 2 is not a hook, it is the payoff of line 1. Never waste it on setup.
No question marks in line 1 unless the question is specific enough that only you could ask it.
Numbers beat adjectives. '$4,200' beats 'a lot of money' every time.
If the hook works with any other person's name on it, it is not your hook.

hooks.name: Contrarian Take
hooks.template: Everyone says {common advice}. After {specific experience}, I think that is wrong.
hooks.example: Everyone says post daily. I posted 4x a week for a year and beat every daily poster in my niche.
hooks.best_for: Establishing a point of view. Highest comment rate of any formula.
hooks.trap: Being contrarian about something nobody believes. The belief has to be genuinely common.

hooks.name: Number Reveal
hooks.template: I {did thing} for {N} {days/weeks}. Here is what actually happened.
hooks.example: I sent 400 cold DMs in 30 days. 11 replied. 2 became clients.
hooks.best_for: Experiments, challenges, anything with a countable result.
hooks.trap: Burying the number. Put it in line 1 or the formula does nothing.

hooks.name: Mistake Confession
hooks.template: {Specific cost} is what {one mistake} cost me.
hooks.example: $18,000 is what not having a contract cost me last March.
hooks.best_for: Trust. People forward the posts where you look bad.
hooks.trap: A fake-humble mistake. 'I care too much' reads as a brag and kills the post.

hooks.name: Before / After
hooks.template: {Time ago} I was {low state}. Today I {high state}. The difference was {one thing}.
hooks.example: 18 months ago I was writing proposals at 2am. Today I send them in 6 minutes. One template did it.
hooks.best_for: Proof you have travelled the distance your reader wants to travel.
hooks.trap: Three-part transformations. Name one lever or the reader stops believing you.

hooks.name: The List Promise
hooks.template: {N} things I wish someone had told me before {milestone}.
hooks.example: 7 things I wish someone had told me before I hired my first employee.
hooks.best_for: Saves. Highest save rate of the 21, which LinkedIn weights heavily.
hooks.trap: N above 10. The reader does not believe you have 15 good ones, and you do not.

hooks.name: Insider Secret
hooks.template: After {N} years {doing thing}, here is the part nobody puts in the {job posting/course/pitch}.
hooks.example: After 9 years in agency sales, here is the part nobody puts in the job posting.
hooks.best_for: Credentialed takes. Works only if the years are real.
hooks.trap: Promising a secret and delivering common knowledge. The comments will say so.

hooks.name: The Callout
hooks.template: If you are still {doing outdated thing}, stop.
hooks.example: If you are still writing your LinkedIn posts in the LinkedIn composer, stop.
hooks.best_for: Short posts with one instruction. Fastest to write of the 21.
hooks.trap: Calling out something nobody does. Or worse, calling out your own audience with contempt.

hooks.name: Question Trap
hooks.template: {Specific scenario with a real cost}. What do you do?
hooks.example: Your best client asks for a 40% discount and hints they will leave without it. What do you do?
hooks.best_for: Comment volume. People answer scenarios, they ignore 'thoughts?'.
hooks.trap: A question with an obvious right answer. There has to be a real fork.

hooks.name: Story Cold Open
hooks.template: "{Line of dialogue}"\n\n{Who said it, when, and why it mattered}.
hooks.example: "We are going with someone cheaper."\n\nThat email arrived 40 minutes after I sent my best proposal of the year.
hooks.best_for: Long-form storytelling posts. Highest dwell time.
hooks.trap: Dialogue nobody would actually say. Use the real line, including the ugly parts.

hooks.name: The Receipt
hooks.template: {Screenshot or hard number}. {One sentence of context}.
hooks.example: 3 clients, 11 days, zero calls booked. Here is the exact sequence that did it.
hooks.best_for: Anything you can prove. Pair with an image and reach roughly doubles.
hooks.trap: A receipt with no story attached. The number opens the door, the story is the room.

hooks.name: Myth Bust
hooks.template: {Popular explanation} is not why {bad outcome} is happening to you.
hooks.example: The algorithm is not why your posts are dying.
hooks.best_for: Reframing. Sets you up to deliver the real cause in line 3.
hooks.trap: Busting the myth and never naming the replacement. Always name it.

hooks.name: The Comparison
hooks.template: {Expensive option} vs {cheap option}. {Surprising verdict}.
hooks.example: A $12,000 brand agency vs a $20 tool and a weekend. The weekend won.
hooks.best_for: Tool and process posts. Very high share rate.
hooks.trap: An unfair comparison. Concede what the expensive option genuinely does better.

hooks.name: Permission Slip
hooks.template: You are allowed to {thing the reader feels guilty about}.
hooks.example: You are allowed to turn down work that pays well and makes you miserable.
hooks.best_for: Reach beyond your niche. These travel further than tactical posts.
hooks.trap: Generic self-care. It has to be specific to the working life of your reader.

hooks.name: Pattern Interrupt
hooks.template: {One word or three-word line, full stop.}
hooks.example: I got fired.
hooks.best_for: Stopping the scroll cold. Whitespace does the work.
hooks.trap: Overuse. Once a month. Every post starting this way reads as a tic.

hooks.name: The Warning
hooks.template: {Common practice} is quietly costing you {specific thing they care about}.
hooks.example: Your 'quick call to align' is quietly costing you six hours a week.
hooks.best_for: Problem-aware audiences who have not connected cause to cost.
hooks.trap: Fear with no exit. Give the fix in the same post or you have just made someone anxious.

hooks.name: Good vs Great
hooks.template: Good {role} {do X}. Great {role} {do Y}.
hooks.example: Good salespeople answer the question. Great salespeople ask why it was asked.
hooks.best_for: Quotable one-liners. Screenshot bait.
hooks.trap: A distinction that is really just 'try harder'. Y has to be a different action, not more effort.

hooks.name: Time Anchor
hooks.template: {Task} used to take me {long time}. It now takes {short time}.
hooks.example: Writing a week of posts used to take me 5 hours. It now takes 20 minutes.
hooks.best_for: Tool, system and automation posts. The strongest hook shape for a how-to.
hooks.trap: An unbelievable ratio. 5 hours to 20 minutes lands. 5 hours to 8 seconds does not.

hooks.name: The Unpopular Rule
hooks.template: I do not {widely accepted practice}. Ever. Here is why.
hooks.example: I do not take discovery calls. Ever.
hooks.best_for: Positioning. Attracts the right clients by repelling the wrong ones.
hooks.trap: A rule you break constantly. Someone in the comments will know.

hooks.name: Curiosity Gap
hooks.template: The {superlative} {thing} I ever {verb} {broke the obvious rule}.
hooks.example: The best hire I ever made failed the interview.
hooks.best_for: Openers that force the 'see more' tap.
hooks.trap: A gap you never close. Pay it off by line 4 or you have written clickbait.

hooks.name: The Walk-Away
hooks.template: I {fired/quit/deleted/cancelled} {valuable thing}. {Result}.
hooks.example: I fired my highest-paying client in January. Revenue is up 30%.
hooks.best_for: Values posts with a business result attached. Very high engagement.
hooks.trap: Walking away with no cost. Name what it actually cost you or it reads as theatre.

hooks.name: The Direct Value
hooks.template: Here is the exact {artifact} I used to {specific outcome}. Steal it.
hooks.example: Here is the exact 4-line email I used to reopen 3 dead deals. Steal it.
hooks.best_for: Lead magnets and comment-for-link posts. Highest conversion of the 21.
hooks.trap: Making them ask for something you could have just posted. Give the artifact away in the post.

profile_rubric.note: Twelve items. Score each honestly - a generous score helps nobody. Most first-pass profiles land in the 30s and 40s.

items.full_marks: States who you help and what changes for them, carries one piece of proof, and is not the job title. Uses the 220 characters, not 60.
First two lines - everything visible before 'see more' - name the reader's problem. No 'passionate about', no third-person bio, no opening with your own name.
Written to one person in second person: their problem, what you do, one number as proof, what to do next. Under 1,400 characters.
Three items: best-performing post, a proof asset, and the way to contact you. Nothing empty, nothing stale.
One line of positioning and one way to reach you. Not the default gradient, not a stock skyline.
Face fills roughly 60% of the frame, eyes visible, shot in the last two years, background not distracting.
One line of scope, then two to three outcome bullets with numbers. Duties are not outcomes.
Last two roles detailed, everything older than ten years compressed to a single line each.
Top three skills are the three you want to be hired for and are endorsed. The other 47 are noise.
At least three received in the last two years, each naming a specific outcome rather than character.
Posted or commented in the last seven days. An empty activity feed reads as an abandoned profile.
Custom URL, a working email or booking link in contact info, and the same handle as your other platforms.

rules: Confirm the title in the first sentence. A hook that ignores its own title is why people leave at 0:08.
One idea. A hook carrying two promises keeps neither.
Specific beats big. '400 to 200,000 in seven months' outperforms 'massive growth'.
Show the artifact inside 20 seconds if you promised one.
Never open with who you are. The subscribe pitch has not been earned yet.

hooks.name: The Statistic
hooks.shape: A number the viewer did not know, stated flat, then the consequence.
hooks.example: 97% of the people who start a channel quit before video 30. Here is what the other 3% do differently.
hooks.fails_when: Dies if the number is vague or unverifiable. Say the source out loud.

hooks.name: Someone Else's Result
hooks.shape: A named person's outcome, then the mechanism.
hooks.example: This channel went from 400 subscribers to 200,000 in seven months on one format. I mapped it.
hooks.fails_when: Do not invent the number. If you cannot name the channel, use a different formula.

hooks.name: The Mistake
hooks.shape: Name the error the viewer is probably making right now.
hooks.example: Your first 30 seconds are why nobody finishes your videos. It is not the topic.
hooks.fails_when: Only works if the mistake is common and the viewer can check it in one second.

hooks.name: Contrarian Flip
hooks.shape: State the accepted advice, then reject it.
hooks.example: Everyone says post daily. I posted once a week for a year and tripled the channel.
hooks.fails_when: Needs evidence in the next 15 seconds or it reads as contrarian for its own sake.

hooks.name: The Reveal
hooks.shape: Promise a specific thing will be shown, then show it.
hooks.example: I am going to show you the exact prompt, on screen, that wrote this video.
hooks.fails_when: You have to actually show it, early. A reveal at 8:00 is a retention cliff at 1:00.

hooks.name: The Superlative
hooks.shape: The single best/worst/fastest of a category.
hooks.example: This is the fastest way to turn one long video into thirty Shorts.
hooks.fails_when: Superlatives are cheap. Earn it by naming what it beat.

hooks.name: The Clock
hooks.shape: Bound the payoff in time.
hooks.example: In the next six minutes you will have a working title, thumbnail and script for your next video.
hooks.fails_when: The clock has to be true. Overrun it and the next video's hook is not believed.

hooks.name: I Tried It
hooks.shape: First-person experiment with a stated cost.
hooks.example: I let an AI run my channel for 30 days. I did not touch the uploads.
hooks.fails_when: Needs a real cost - time, money, risk - or there is no stake.

hooks.name: The Question
hooks.shape: Ask the exact question the viewer typed into search.
hooks.example: Why do your videos die at 30 seconds when the topic is fine?
hooks.fails_when: Must be the viewer's question, not yours. Pull it from your own comments.

hooks.name: Before and After
hooks.shape: Two states, one cut between them.
hooks.example: This was my thumbnail. This is my thumbnail now. Same video, four times the click-through.
hooks.fails_when: Only works with a visual. Do not use it on a talking-head-only video.

hooks.name: The Teardown
hooks.shape: Take a real thing apart in public.
hooks.example: I pulled the nine most-viewed AI videos of the month and broke down what the titles share.
hooks.fails_when: Name what you pulled and how many. A teardown of one example is an anecdote.

hooks.name: The Stack
hooks.shape: Two named tools combined into one outcome.
hooks.example: Claude plus your YouTube Studio export gives you next week's upload schedule in one prompt.
hooks.fails_when: Both tools must be nameable and the outcome must need both.

hooks.name: The Warning
hooks.shape: A cost the viewer is about to pay.
hooks.example: Do not upload another video until you check this one setting.
hooks.fails_when: If the cost is small the hook is a lie. Reserve it.

hooks.name: The List
hooks.shape: A counted set, with the count in the first line.
hooks.example: Seven things I would do differently if I started a channel in 2026.
hooks.fails_when: The count must be exact and every item must be different in kind.

hooks.name: The Receipt
hooks.shape: Show the artifact first, explain second.
hooks.example: This is the analytics page. This video did 40% of the channel's watch time. Here is why.
hooks.fails_when: Requires a real screenshot. A described receipt is not a receipt.

hooks.name: The Insider
hooks.shape: Information from inside a system.
hooks.example: YouTube tells you which videos are underperforming. Almost nobody opens the report.
hooks.fails_when: Do not claim insider access you do not have.

hooks.name: The Impossible Claim
hooks.shape: State something that sounds untrue, then prove it.
hooks.example: You can write, title, thumbnail and schedule a week of videos without opening a single editor.
hooks.fails_when: The proof has to start within 20 seconds or it reads as clickbait.

hooks.name: The Comparison
hooks.shape: Two named options, one winner.
hooks.example: I wrote the same video three ways. One of them held 62% and the other two did not.
hooks.fails_when: Say the losing option out loud. A comparison with no loser is an advert.

hooks.name: The Origin
hooks.shape: Where a result actually came from.
hooks.example: Every video on this channel starts in the same 12-line file. Here it is.
hooks.fails_when: Works once per channel. It is a reveal about you, and you only have one.

hooks.name: The Deadline
hooks.shape: Something is changing on a date.
hooks.example: The old description format stops mattering this month. Here is what replaces it.
hooks.fails_when: Only use with a real, checkable date. This is the fastest formula to lose trust with.

hooks.name: The Direct Address
hooks.shape: Name the exact viewer in the first six words.
hooks.example: If you have under a thousand subscribers, this is the only video you need this week.
hooks.fails_when: Narrow beats broad. 'If you make videos' addresses nobody.

rules: Write the spoken line and the on-screen line separately. On screen is the shorter, blunter one, six words or fewer, no punctuation it does not need.
No setup. The video starts at the sentence you would normally reach at second six.
Say the number. 'A lot' is not a number and neither is 'so much time'.
The first frame is a hook too. A static talking head at 0:00 with no motion and no text is three hooks wasted.
If the hook would work for anyone else in your niche, it is not your hook. Put the thing only you can say in it.
A hook promises something. Deliver it before the halfway mark or the retention you bought gets handed back.

hooks.name: Cost Confession
hooks.template: {Specific amount} is what {one mistake} cost me.
hooks.example: $18,000 is what one missing clause cost me.
hooks.best_for: Trust, fast. People finish the videos where you are the one who looks bad.
hooks.trap: A fake cost. 'It cost me my peace of mind' is not a number and everybody can hear that.

hooks.name: Negative Command
hooks.template: Stop {common action}. Do {alternative} instead.
hooks.example: Stop posting three times a day. Post twice and reply to every comment for an hour.
hooks.best_for: Saves and arguments. The imperative gets attention that a statement does not.
hooks.trap: Telling people to stop doing something nobody does. The habit has to be one the viewer recognises in themselves.

hooks.name: Nobody Tells You
hooks.template: Nobody tells you that {uncomfortable truth about the thing they want}.
hooks.example: Nobody tells you that your first 30 reels are supposed to flop.
hooks.best_for: New audiences. It positions you as the person who says the quiet part.
hooks.trap: Picking a truth everybody already says. If the comments are agreeing before you finish, it was not a secret.

hooks.name: The Replacement
hooks.template: {This thing} replaced {expensive thing} for {price}.
hooks.example: This $12 tool replaced the editor I was paying $2,000 a month.
hooks.best_for: Demos and tool videos. The price gap does the work.
hooks.trap: Overstating the replacement. If it replaced 60% of the job, say 60%, or the comments will say it for you.

hooks.name: Time Collapse
hooks.template: This used to take me {long time}. It now takes {short time}.
hooks.example: Proposals used to take me five hours. They take twenty minutes now.
hooks.best_for: Process videos where the payoff is speed. Reads instantly on screen.
hooks.trap: A ratio nobody believes. 40 hours to 4 seconds gets treated as a lie even when it is true.

hooks.name: The Receipt
hooks.template: I {did thing} for {N days}. Here are the actual numbers.
hooks.example: I posted one reel a day for 60 days. Here is what it did to my DMs.
hooks.best_for: Experiments. Pairs with a screen recording of the real dashboard, which is the whole value.
hooks.trap: Not showing the screen. A numbers video with no screen recording is a numbers claim.

hooks.name: Wrong Way, Right Way
hooks.template: You are doing {thing} wrong, and it is not your fault. {The fix}.
hooks.example: You are writing captions wrong, and it is not your fault. Instagram hides everything after line one.
hooks.best_for: Teaching. The 'not your fault' half stops it reading as an insult, which is what kills this one.
hooks.trap: Skipping the absolution. 'You are doing it wrong' on its own makes people leave rather than learn.

hooks.name: Insider Leak
hooks.template: I spent {N years} {inside the thing}. Here is what we never said out loud.
hooks.example: I spent six years selling agency retainers. Here is what we never put in the proposal.
hooks.best_for: Authority without a credential slide. Works only if the years are real.
hooks.trap: Promising a secret and delivering the brochure. The comments are merciless about this one.

hooks.name: The Steal
hooks.template: Steal this {artifact}. It took me {time} to get right.
hooks.example: Steal this four-line follow-up. It took me two years and a lot of dead leads.
hooks.best_for: Saves and sends, which are the two metrics that move reach the most.
hooks.trap: The artifact not being on screen. If they cannot screenshot it, there is nothing to steal.

hooks.name: If This, Then Watch
hooks.template: If you {specific situation}, this {short time} fixes it.
hooks.example: If your reels get views and no followers, the next 40 seconds fix it.
hooks.best_for: Qualifying hard. Fewer people stay, and the ones who do are the ones who buy.
hooks.trap: A situation so broad it qualifies nobody. 'If you want to grow' is not a situation.

hooks.name: Numbered With A Favourite
hooks.template: {N} {things} that {outcome}. Number {k} is the one nobody uses.
hooks.example: Five caption edits that double saves. Number four is the one nobody does.
hooks.best_for: Retention through the middle: naming a favourite gives people a reason to stay past three.
hooks.trap: N above seven. Nobody believes you have nine good ones, and you do not.

hooks.name: The Objection
hooks.template: "{Objection they actually say}." Fine. Here is the version that works anyway.
hooks.example: "I don't want to be on camera." Fine. Here is the faceless version that still sells.
hooks.best_for: Selling to the people who already said no once.
hooks.trap: Inventing the objection. Pull it verbatim from a DM or a comment, including the bad grammar.

hooks.name: Before And After, On Screen
hooks.template: {Show the old thing}. {Show the new thing}. {One sentence on the lever}.
hooks.example: This was my profile in March. This is it now. I changed the name field, nothing else.
hooks.best_for: Anything visual. The cut between the two frames is the hook, the words are secondary.
hooks.trap: Three levers. Name one thing that changed or the transformation stops being believable.

hooks.name: The Callout
hooks.template: {Specific group}, this is the one you have been ignoring.
hooks.example: Photographers charging under $2,000: this is the pricing page you have been avoiding.
hooks.best_for: Cutting a broad audience down to the one that converts. Send rate goes up because people tag each other.
hooks.trap: A group so large it is not a callout. 'Entrepreneurs' is not a group.

hooks.name: The Flop Record
hooks.template: My first {N} {attempts} did nothing. Here is what changed on {N+1}.
hooks.example: My first 47 reels averaged 300 views. Number 48 did 400,000. One thing was different.
hooks.best_for: People at the start, which is most of the audience. High comment rate.
hooks.trap: Making the change sound like luck. If the answer is 'I got lucky', there is no video.

hooks.name: The Verbatim Question
hooks.template: "{Question exactly as it was asked}" - I get this every week.
hooks.example: "How do I post consistently without hating it?" I get this one every week.
hooks.best_for: Search. A question typed the way people type it is what Instagram search is matching against.
hooks.trap: Tidying the question up. The value is that it is in their words, typos and all.

hooks.name: Head To Head
hooks.template: {A} versus {B}. I ran both for {time} and one of them was not close.
hooks.example: Carousels versus reels. I ran both for 90 days and it was not close.
hooks.best_for: Comments. People arrive already holding an opinion, which is the point.
hooks.trap: Refusing to pick. A comparison with a diplomatic ending is a video with no ending.

hooks.name: Cold Open Demo
hooks.template: {Start mid-action, already doing the thing.} Watch what this does.
hooks.example: Watch what happens when I paste a competitor's caption into this.
hooks.best_for: Screen recordings and anything with a visible result. No setup at all, the hand is already moving.
hooks.trap: A result that takes twelve seconds to arrive. If the payoff is slow, cut to it and show the wait afterwards.

hooks.name: The Deadline
hooks.template: {Thing} changes on {date}. Do {action} before then.
hooks.example: Your top nine grid crops change the second you post a reel. Fix the covers first.
hooks.best_for: Urgency that is real. Platform changes, seasonal windows, policy updates.
hooks.trap: Manufactured urgency. One fake deadline and every future one is discounted.

hooks.name: Permission
hooks.template: You do not need {the thing everyone says you need}.
hooks.example: You do not need a niche. You need one person you can name.
hooks.best_for: Relief. Very high save rate, because it removes a blocker rather than adding a task.
hooks.trap: Removing the blocker and putting nothing in its place. The second half is the whole video.

hooks.name: Mid-Sentence Start
hooks.template: {...and that is when {the turn}.}
hooks.example: ...and that is when the client asked for the money back. Three days after approving it.
hooks.best_for: Stories. Starting mid-scene makes the viewer feel they arrived late, which is a reason to stay.
hooks.trap: Never going back to fill in the gap. Deliver the setup by second eight or it reads as a mistake.

hooks.name: Contrarian Flip
hooks.template: {Well-known saying, inverted.}
hooks.example: Nice guys finish first.
hooks.best_for: Comments. The viewer has to stop and check whether they misheard you.
hooks.trap: Flipping a saying nobody says. The original has to be a reflex, or the inversion is just a sentence.

hooks.name: The Statistic
hooks.template: {N}% of {group} {surprising fact}.
hooks.example: 33% of high school graduates never read another book.
hooks.best_for: Sends. A number a person can repeat at dinner gets sent to somebody.
hooks.trap: A statistic you cannot source. Say where it came from in the video or do not use it.

hooks.name: The Reveal
hooks.template: This is the new {thing}.
hooks.example: This is the new Sony point and shoot, and it fixes the one thing I hated.
hooks.best_for: Anything physical or visual. The object is the hook and the words are captions on it.
hooks.trap: Holding the thing up without saying what it changes. A reveal with no stake is an advert.

hooks.name: Someone Else's Result
hooks.template: There was one {person} who {outcome} in {time}.
hooks.example: There was one creator who grew a million subscribers in a single month.
hooks.best_for: Proof when the user does not have their own number yet. Third-person is allowed if it is true.
hooks.trap: No name and no link. An anonymous miracle is a rumour.

hooks.name: The Superlative
hooks.template: The {fastest / biggest / only} {thing} is {the answer}.
hooks.example: The fastest way to get confident is to build evidence you cannot argue with.
hooks.best_for: One-claim videos with no story attached. It is the most common shape in the wild and the easiest to write badly.
hooks.trap: A superlative with a soft answer. If the second half is 'consistency', you have said nothing and the comments will tell you.

structures.name: "Not only X but also Y"
structures.fix: Split into two sentences, or drop the weaker half.

structures.name: "It isn't about X. It's about Y."
structures.fix: Lead with Y. The reversal is the tell.

structures.name: One-word rhetorical question line
structures.fix: Answer it inline instead of staging a reveal.

structures.name: "Here's what I learned"
structures.fix: State the lesson. Skip the announcement.

structures.name: Rule-of-three triad
structures.fix: Two items or four. Three is the model's default rhythm.

structures.name: Rocket / fire / bulb / sparkle / dart emoji
structures.fix: One emoji max, and not one of these five.

structures.name: Hashtag wall (5+)
structures.fix: Three hashtags. LinkedIn stopped rewarding the wall.

structures.name: Model self-reference
structures.fix: Delete the sentence.

structures.name: Essay-closer opener
structures.fix: A post does not need a conclusion paragraph.

structures.name: Reflex engagement bait
structures.fix: Ask a question only you could ask, about the specific thing above it.

structures.name: "Stop scrolling" opener
structures.fix: The scroll-stop has to be the claim itself. Asking for attention is the tell that you have not earned it.

structures.regex: (?i)\b(?:in (?:this|today'?s) (?:video|reel|post)|today i'?m going to show you|i'?m going to (?:show|teach) you how)\b
structures.name: Video preamble ("in this video I'm going to show you")
structures.fix: Delete it and start at the payoff. The first two seconds decide the whole reel.

structures.name: Emoji bullet list
structures.fix: Use a hyphen or a line break. Emoji bullets are the single most template-looking thing in a caption.

structures.name: Three or more shouted words in a row
structures.fix: Caps are a volume knob, not a highlighter. One word, at most.

structures.regex: (?i)\b(?:follow for more|tag someone who|double tap if|share this if|comment below if)\b
structures.name: Reflex follow or tag bait
structures.fix: Ask for the one action this post actually earns. The generic ask trains the audience to ignore every ask.

profile_rubric.note: Twelve items. Score each honestly - a generous score helps nobody. Most first-pass profiles land in the 30s and 40s. The weighting is deliberate: the name field, the first bio line and the pinned three are worth more than the photo, because they are what a stranger who arrived from one reel actually processes before deciding to follow.

items.full_marks: The name field (30 characters, the bold line, not the handle) carries the name plus what they do in words people search: 'Dana Ruiz | Proposal templates'. This field is indexed by Instagram search and most accounts waste it on a name alone.
items.common_fail: Just a name, or a name with an emoji.

items.full_marks: Line one names who this is for and what changes for them, in their words. Not a job title, not a list of adjectives, not three emoji separated by bars.
The rest of the 150 characters carries one piece of proof or one specific offer, and reads as sentences rather than a pipe-separated list.

Three posts pinned to the top of the grid, doing three different jobs: the best proof, the clearest explanation of the offer, and the best introduction to the person. Not the three highest-view posts by accident.
items.common_fail: Nothing pinned, so the top of the grid is whatever was posted last.

items.full_marks: One destination that matches what the bio just promised. Up to five links are allowed; more than two is a menu, and a menu converts worse than a door.
items.common_fail: A link tree with eleven options, or no link at all.

items.full_marks: Four to six highlights named for the questions a buyer actually asks: Pricing, Results, How it works, About. Covers consistent. Nothing older than a year sitting at the front.
The first nine covers are legible at thumbnail size and say what the account is about without a single tap. Reel covers are chosen deliberately, not left as frame one.
items.common_fail: Nine covers of a face mid-word with no text.

items.full_marks: Face fills roughly 60% of a circle that renders at about 40 pixels. Eyes visible, shot in the last two years, background not competing.
items.common_fail: A full-body shot, a logo for a personal brand, or a photo taken at arm's length in a dark room.

items.full_marks: Readable, sayable out loud, and the same handle as the other platforms. No stacked underscores or numbers standing in for letters.
items.common_fail: A handle nobody can spell after hearing it once.

items.full_marks: Professional account with a category that matches the offer, and contact buttons that work. Email that is checked, not the one from 2019.
items.common_fail: Personal account, so there are no insights and no contact button.

items.full_marks: Posted in the last seven days and replied to comments on the most recent post. An account that last posted in March reads as closed.
items.common_fail: A five-week gap, or a wall of unanswered comments.

items.full_marks: A story up right now, or at least most days. It is the difference between a profile and a person.

reel_structure.0-3s: Visual Pattern Interrupt + Spoken Hook (<= 6 words on screen)

families.why: Vagueness makes the model guess. Wrong guesses force retries, and every retry resends the full conversation.

patterns.name: no deliverable named
patterns.signal: The prompt says what topic to work on but not what to produce (a table? a script? a file? a list?).
patterns.fix: Name the artifact: 'one table with columns X, Y, Z', 'a 30-second script', 'a single .md file'.

patterns.name: no audience
patterns.signal: Content is requested with no reader in mind ('write me something for instagram').
patterns.fix: Say who it is for and what they already know: 'a local coffee shop with 8k followers'.

patterns.name: no length or size
patterns.signal: No word count, item count, or duration, so the model picks one and it is wrong.
patterns.fix: Cap it: 'under 400 words', '10 ideas', '3 options max'.

patterns.name: no done-when
patterns.signal: There is no way to tell whether the answer succeeded.
patterns.fix: State the finish line: 'done when I can paste it into the scheduler without edits'.

patterns.name: 'something like' hedging
patterns.signal: 'something like', 'kind of', 'maybe a', 'or whatever' in the ask.
patterns.fix: Commit to one version. You can change it after you see it.

patterns.name: open verdict fishing
patterns.signal: 'thoughts?', 'what do you think?', 'any ideas?' with no decision attached.
patterns.fix: Ask the decision you actually face: 'pick one of these two and say why'.

patterns.name: style matters but no example
patterns.signal: Tone or format matters and no sample is given, guaranteeing a voice miss.
patterns.fix: Paste one short example of the style you want and say 'match this'.

patterns.name: buried constraint
patterns.signal: A hard requirement you already know (budget, tool, deadline) is left out, then revealed after the first wrong answer.
patterns.fix: List every known constraint up front, even the obvious ones.

patterns.name: multiple unrelated asks fused
patterns.signal: Two or three different jobs in one sentence, so each gets a shallow half-answer.
patterns.fix: One prompt per job, or number them and ask for them in order.

patterns.name: 'make it better' with no direction
patterns.signal: Improvement is requested without naming what is wrong.
patterns.fix: Name the failure: 'the hook is weak', 'too formal', 'cut it to half'.

families.why: Saying the same thing twice is pure waste. The second explanation costs tokens and proves the first one leaked.

patterns.name: re-pasting the same context
patterns.signal: The same background paragraph gets pasted into message after message.
patterns.fix: State it once, lock it as a decision, and reference it ('per the locked voice').

patterns.name: restarting instead of continuing
patterns.signal: A fresh chat is opened for a follow-up, so all context must be rebuilt from zero.
patterns.fix: Continue the thread, or carry a 5-line summary + the locked decisions into the new one.

patterns.name: repeating a decision already made
patterns.signal: A preference stated earlier (voice, format, stack) is restated because the model drifted.
patterns.fix: Lock it in decisions.md the first time. Locked decisions are re-applied automatically.

patterns.name: asking the model to recall its own output
patterns.signal: 'like you said before' or 'use the version from earlier' with no quote, forcing a re-derivation.
patterns.fix: Paste the 2 lines you mean. Quoting is cheaper than remembering.

patterns.name: unstated correction loop
patterns.signal: The same class of mistake gets corrected one instance at a time across many messages.
patterns.fix: Correct the rule, not the instance: 'never use em dashes anywhere', then lock it.

families.why: Every pasted token is billed on every following turn. Context you did not need is rent you keep paying.

patterns.name: whole file for a one-function question
patterns.signal: 800 lines pasted when the question is about 20.
patterns.fix: Paste the relevant function plus its callers. Name the file for the rest.

patterns.name: unsummarized transcript dump
patterns.signal: A full meeting transcript or thread pasted raw when only the decisions matter.
patterns.fix: Ask for or write a 10-line summary first, then work from that.

patterns.name: irrelevant attachments
patterns.signal: Docs attached 'just in case' that the task never touches.
patterns.fix: Attach only what the task reads. Mention the rest exists.

patterns.name: screenshot of text
patterns.signal: An error message or config sent as an image, which costs more and reads worse.
patterns.fix: Paste the text itself. Exact characters matter.

patterns.name: paraphrased error message
patterns.signal: 'it says something about a missing module' instead of the actual error.
patterns.fix: Paste the exact error, top line to bottom line.

patterns.name: duplicated instructions
patterns.signal: The same rule appears in the prompt twice in different words, inviting the model to treat them as different rules.
patterns.fix: Say each rule once, in one place.

patterns.name: redundant context
patterns.signal: Background the model already has (from this chat, the repo, or a locked decision) is pasted again anyway.
patterns.fix: Trust what is already in context. Add only what is new.

families.why: When the how is open, the model picks a how. If its pick is wrong you pay for the work twice.

patterns.name: no stack or tool pinned
patterns.signal: A build is requested without naming the language, framework, or tool, so the model chooses and gets corrected.
patterns.fix: Pin it: 'plain HTML + vanilla JS, no frameworks'.

patterns.name: no do-not-touch list
patterns.signal: Nothing marks what must stay unchanged, so working parts get rewritten.
patterns.fix: Say what is frozen: 'do not modify the deploy script or the schema'.

patterns.name: missing environment facts
patterns.signal: OS, versions, or account limits that change the answer are left for the model to assume.
patterns.fix: State them: 'macOS, Node 22, free-tier plan'.

patterns.name: full rewrite when a diff would do
patterns.signal: 'rewrite the whole thing' for a 2-line change, regenerating everything.
patterns.fix: Ask for the edit: 'change only the hook, keep the rest verbatim'.

patterns.name: no output cap on long generation
patterns.signal: An open-ended 'write everything' that produces 3x more than will be read.
patterns.fix: Cap the output and ask for the rest only if needed.

patterns.name: no priority when tradeoffs exist
patterns.signal: Speed, cost, and quality all implied equally, so the model optimizes the wrong one.
patterns.fix: Rank them: 'fast and cheap beats polished here'.

families.why: Messages are the unit of waste. Five turns that could have been one means the context got re-billed five times.

patterns.name: one-question drip
patterns.signal: Related questions asked one message at a time instead of batched.
patterns.fix: Batch them: number 4 questions in one message, get 4 answers in one pass.

patterns.name: permission-seeking turn
patterns.signal: 'can you...?' / 'would it be possible to...?' as its own message before the real ask.
patterns.fix: Just ask the real thing. The capability check is free inside the same message.

patterns.name: resending everything to change one word
patterns.signal: The full prompt is re-pasted with a tiny edit instead of stating the delta.
patterns.fix: Send the delta: 'same as before but the audience is beginners'.

patterns.name: vague rejection
patterns.signal: 'not quite' / 'didn't like it' with no named miss, forcing a blind second attempt.
patterns.fix: Name the miss in one line, and say what to keep.

patterns.name: politeness padding
patterns.signal: Apologies, warm-ups, and sign-offs carrying zero instruction, re-billed every turn after.
patterns.fix: Be direct. Spend the tokens on constraints instead.

families.why: Some turns should never have been prompts at all.

patterns.name: big model for a lookup
patterns.signal: A frontier model asked to spell-check, convert units, or fetch a fact a smaller tool answers.
patterns.fix: Route trivial turns to a small model or a plain tool. Save the big model for judgment.

patterns.name: regenerate instead of edit
patterns.signal: Rerolling the whole answer hoping the one flaw disappears.
patterns.fix: Point at the flaw and ask for a targeted fix of that section only.

blueprints.title: agent-progress-theater — Agent Progress Theater
blueprints.content:
# agent-progress-theater — Agent Progress Theater

**intent**: Agent work performed as WORKING-STATE theater — a short trigger beat hands the frame to the machine, which then visibly _works_: loaders spin, status phrases swap, dots pulse, counters tick — before the receipt arrives as a card whose rows cascade in and CHANGE STATE (badges flip to checks, labels strike through, severity pills read out), or as a conversation thread building message-by-message onto a camera push-in payoff. The subject is the machine performing labor over time. It is NOT a typed prompt awaiting output (no prompt/input is ever typed — the trigger is a click, a menu choice, or an already-running scan); NOT `cursor-ui-demo` (at most ONE igniting click here, then the cursor exits and the UI performs itself); NOT `grid-card-assemble` (rows there assemble into a static enumeration and hold — rows here are alive: they arrive as agent output and then MUTATE, checking off one by one while the viewer watches).

**roles served**

- Key_Feature (from `agent-progress-theater`): when the feature is the agent doing multi-step work (build a plan / scan a repo / fix a vulnerability / handle infra for you) and the proof is status theater — a loader lockup with a typed label, status couplets swapping under an `[accent]` spinner, then a checklist/findings card that populates and checks off in front of the viewer.
- Key_Feature (from `message-thread-payoff`): when the agent's work lives inside a conversation or automation thread — user/agent bubbles and tool-call/reply cards popping in sequence, the working state carried by pulsing loading dots or rapidly ticking diff counters, resolved by ONE camera push-in tight on the confirmation line (`[reaction pill]`, "Sent using `[@Bot]`", a thank-you bubble).

**duration**: 4.2–11.6s (short members are a single card-and-check-off or thread beat at ~4–5s; long members chain trigger → interstitial → status swaps → receipt card at ~9–12s; thread payoff spans 4.2–9.1s)

blueprints.title: camera-journey — Camera Journey
blueprints.content:
# camera-journey — Camera Journey

**intent**: The real viewport camera is the STORYTELLER — a multi-leg journey (dive in → a mid-journey beat fires → travel to the consequence / reposition → landing push, at rest) across ONE continuous world, where the travel itself carries the narrative. Two folded sub-shapes: **(A) action roundtrip** — the camera dives into a UI panel, a cursor/typed action fires, and the camera swoops/pans to another region where the consequence renders as element motion; **(B) cursorless flight** — pure cinematic 3D flight (motion blur, depth-of-field, tilt-to-flatten rotations) over static or self-animating content, no cursor anywhere.

**boundary**: This is NOT `cursor-ui-demo` — there the camera _chases_ the cursor (a servo following the actor); here the camera IS the actor, moving on its own narrative motivation, and in sub-shape A the cursor acts only at the leg hinge (in B it never appears). This is NOT `device-surface-showcase` — there one DEVICE/surface is hero and the camera merely presents it; here no single surface is hero — the journey traverses multiple regions/panels/depth planes and the traversal is the story. This is NOT `spatial-pan-stations` — there pre-placed stations on a flat canvas are visited by repeated pans of the same type; here the legs are heterogeneous (push-in, swoop, pull-back-rotate, whip, dive) and each leg is _motivated_ (by a fired action, or by the reveal it lands on).

**roles served**

- Benefits (from `camera-swoop-panel-action-roundtrip`): when the benefit IS a cause→effect round trip — "do this small thing here, get this big thing there" (comment → chart morphs; agent finding → verified commit; chat message → receipt + ledger). The camera physically connects the action to its payoff, so the viewer _travels_ the value chain instead of being told it.
- Key_Feature (from `cursorless-camera-flight`): when the feature should feel cinematic and inevitable — a payout form or a generated content-plan calendar ex

**intent**: Two paired items of equal weight shown side-by-side with mirrored 3D "book-open" tilts — the eye reads them as a balanced comparison, then a pill badge lands at each card's inner edge to punctuate. The motion IS the symmetry: two cards arriving from opposite wings into a held spread.

**roles served**

- Key_Feature (from `comparison-split-cards`): when two complementary features / capabilities of equal weight should be presented **simultaneously, not sequentially** — an A/B, a "X + Y together," paired concepts the viewer must weigh side-by-side. blueprints.content:
# cta-morph-press — CTA Morph & Press

**intent**: A resting brand mark condenses at the same screen center into a smaller, brighter CTA, then a cursor arrives from off-stage and lands a human-aimed click on it. The viewer's eye is walked from "this is who we are" to "and this is what you do." The morph and the click are the two headline beats.

**roles served**

- CTA (from `cta-morph-press`): when the close moves from brand identity to a single user action, two elements share the same center sequentially (a morph, not a cut), and the payoff is a simulated click with physical feedback. Reach for it for a focused "click here" sign-off — no spatial set, no multi-step UI (that's `cursor-ui-demo`).
- Hook (ROLE-WIDENED, from `widget-morph-on-blank-field`): the same
  machinery run as an OPENER — a lone `[widget]` (pill / chip lockup) on a flat field transforms
  in place, performs its payload, then vanishes to a plain frame that a typed `[title]` resolves.
  The click, when present, ignites the morph rather than closing it; there may be no cursor at
  all. Reach for it when the product hook IS one widget doing one thing — still no spatial set,
  no multi-step UI (that's `cursor-ui-demo`). Mint-reconsideration trigger: if future mining
  brings 2+ more widget-morph openers with the vanish → typed-title resolve, promote this variant
  to its own blueprint (the beat order is fully inverted by then).

**duration**: 4–6s (Hook widget-morph opener 5–7.5s)

**shot structure** (a `[bg]` canvas; hero and CTA are flex-centered siblings sharing one `transform-origin`)

- **Scene 1 (0.0–~1.4s) — presence.** The `[hero mark / brand lockup]` holds dead-center, alive but resting — only a faint rotational breath on the mark; any title text under it stays rock-stable. Camera static.
- **Scene 2 (~1.4–2.4s) — the morph (signature move).** The hero CONDENSES at the same screen center into a smaller, brighter `[CTA]` (button / card): the outgoing mark shrink-fades exactly as the CTA scale

blueprints.content:
# dataviz-countup — Data-Viz / Count-Up

**intent**: Make numbers and charts the hero — a count-up ring/number, a trend chart, a tilted stat/card grid — and traverse the data instruments with a camera that pushes THROUGH them (or scrolls across them) to land on one hero metric, so the data itself carries the argument.

**roles served**

- Problem (from `problem-dataviz-pushthrough`): quantifies the pain with real-looking instruments — a count-up ring → a trend chart → a stat grid — the camera pushing THROUGH each object into the next to dramatize a worsening / large-scale problem ("X% of people struggle with…").

blueprints.content:
# device-surface-showcase — Device / Surface Showcase

**intent**: A product surface — a device mockup or a floating browser/app window — is the hero held in frame while its screens cycle through a real flow, showcased by a camera move that ranges from a static hold to a continuous 3D push.

**roles served**

- Key_Feature (from key-feature-device-screen-tour, key-feature-floating-window-scroll, key-feature-3d-device-hand-demo): show a feature being \_experienced inside its real interface\* — the surface houses the action and its screens advance through a flow, rather than enumerating tiles or chasing a cursor across a workflow. (Note: the three founding drafts are Key_Feature and variants differ by MECHANIC, not role; the mined stepwise-flow variant widens the blueprint to Product_Intro.)
- Key_Feature (from demo-page-scroll-spotlight): the floating-window push-scroll variant carried to a spotlight climax — a real webpage rendered as a tilted 3D card coasts in (power2, like a phone held up — no spring), header keywords flare on a karaoke glow as the VO names them, the page rolls to the demoed section, and one element LIFTS off the surface (translateZ + scale) under a radial spotlight that dims the rest.
- Product_Intro (from stepwise-flow-completion): a compact end-to-end product flow — setup/auth → action → success/confirm — plays out cursorless as successive screen states inside the held surface, capped by a confirming button press; bookended by title-card beats. The surface introduces the product by \_completing its core loop\*, not by touring screens.
- Key_Feature (from `showcase-carousel`): the showcase-carousel — two surfaces in sequence (a widget card cycling brand skins, a phone frame with app screens sliding through it) gated by interstitial claim words; the screen cycle is a breadth carousel ("N brands / N apps"), not a flow.

**intent**: A context phrase types in, an accent word cycles through options like a slot-machine to suggest "this could be many things," then a hero CRASHES in from off-screen and physically shoves the text aside — "actually, this is what it is." A collision, not a fade.
